title: Boolean Matching Reversible Circuits: Algorithm and Complexity
problem: Given two black-box reversible logic circuits promised to be matchable, determine their equivalences under various input/output negation and permutation conditions. This is the first formal treatment of Boolean matching for reversible circuits.
motivation: Boolean matching is critical for logic synthesis and verification; extending it to reversible circuits enables design automation and verification for quantum circuit synthesis applications.
method: Develops algorithms to check equivalence under different conditions: with/without access to inverse circuits, with input-only negation/permutation, and with both input/output negations. Provides a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for the input negation/permutation case while establishing exponential classical lower bounds, and derives complexity-theoretic hardness results for other variants.
key_novelty: First study of Boolean matching for reversible circuits, providing the first demonstration of quantum exponential speedup in design automation problems.
contributions: First formal treatment of Boolean matching for reversible circuits
Quantum polynomial-time algorithm for equivalence under input negation and permutation
Exponential quantum speedup versus exponential classical lower bound proof
Hardness result: equivalence with both input/output negations requires UNIQUE-SAT

metrics.speedup: exponential (quantum polynomial vs classical exponential for input negation case)
metrics.other: Complexity-theoretic hardness results for output negation variant

limitations: Limitations not discussed; provides theoretical complexity results without empirical implementation or experimental validation on realistic circuits.
primary_theme: Quantum complexity of reversible circuit equivalence
